headline: NQ is in its second night of the CME weekend halt with no live price path anywhere in the 24-hour horizon: Tail stays low at 9% and EA_ON, while Stress holds elevated at 45% on a day-168 Hormuz closure, a 5-6% weekly oil rally now compounded by a drone strike halting Russian exports at Novorossiysk, a sharp July retail-sales and sentiment miss, and an unprecedented U.S. Iran sanctions package explicitly flagged for next week.
statusText: CME equity-index futures have been shut since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and do not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, so there is no observable price path this hour and none anywhere in the 24-hour horizon, which ends at 01:00 UTC on 16 August - still some 21 hours before the reopen. Tail is 9% (low), holding the action at EA_ON and the status green: pathological one-way structure cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than any observed extension. Friday's re-verified close supports that reading - the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,046.14, down 38.36 points or 0.13%, mid-range inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 band and about 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20, with VIX at 14.25 (-2.60%) after a contained 14.18-14.72 day range. Stress is 45% (elevated) and is deliberately held far above the 9-14% weekend floor used in earlier halt runs, because the volatility backdrop is unresolved rather than merely dormant: the Strait of Hormuz is in roughly its 168th day of effective closure, WTI settled at $82.40 and Brent at $88.52 for weekly gains of 5.4% and 6.0%, a drone attack suspended crude exports from Russia's Sheskharis terminal at Novorossiysk, July retail sales fell 0.6% month-on-month against +0.1% expected, University of Michigan preliminary August sentiment collapsed to 51.0 from 55.2, a 30-year Treasury auction cleared at 5.216% - the highest in 25 years - and Treasury Secretary Bessent has said the administration will unveil measures 'like have never been seen in the history of economic isolation of a country' next week. Confidence is 58% (medium-low), a touch above last hour: index levels, VIX with its day range, oil with precise weekly changes, Federal Reserve H.15 constant maturities and the full 17-21 August U.S. calendar were all re-read from primary sources this hour, but the single most important input - live price structure - is unobservable for the entire horizon, and three intended sources returned 403, which together cap the reading below the solid band.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (9%) alone. With no venue quoting anywhere in the 24-hour horizon there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window, and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it. The operative checkpoint is the CME Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August, where accumulated weekend headlines would express as an opening gap rather than as intraday structure; the danger window brackets that reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery. The gap risk is genuinely two-way: the Iran economic-isolation package is now confirmed for next week alongside an indefinite blockade, while Iran ties any Hormuz reopening to an end to that blockade and to sanctions relief - either thread can move oil and risk appetite before Monday. Do not assume continuity with Friday's calm close through that gap; re-score on observed evidence once price discovery resumes. The next scheduled macro checkpoint is the Empire State survey on 17 August at 12:30 UTC, with FOMC Minutes on 19 August at 18:00 UTC the only high-impact event in the seven-day window. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active throughout. This is a general market assessment for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and it is not a recommendation to place any trade.
body:
No live price path is available this hour. CME equity-index futures closed for the weekend at Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and do not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, so directional efficiency, pullback depth, repeated extension and proximity to session extremes are all unobservable for the whole of the current 24-hour horizon. Everything below is the last confirmed state plus corroborated news, and that limitation - not a judgement that markets are calm - is what caps Confidence below the solid band.

Last confirmed structure (Friday 14 August U.S. cash session, re-verified this hour): the Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,046.14, down 38.36 points or 0.13%, against a 30,084.50 previous close, inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 session range and roughly 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20 (52-week range 22,841.42-30,762.20). Closing mid-range rather than pinned at an extreme is the single most important structural fact available, and it argues directly against pathological one-way structure. The S&P 500 closed at 7,785.76 (-0.17%), the Nasdaq Composite at 26,729.16 (-0.28%) and the Dow at 53,732.41 (-0.20%), all slipping from Thursday's record close while still capping a third consecutive weekly gain. Breadth actively contradicts a large-cap breakdown: the Russell 2000 rose 0.51% to 3,068.42 and notched a fresh record while the megacap indices fell, so Friday was rotation rather than de-risking. VIX closed at 14.25, down 0.38 or 2.60% from 14.63, having traded only 14.18-14.72 - a level and a range entirely inconsistent with a stressed or one-way tape.

Macro was the drag, and it was a genuine miss on both prints: July retail sales fell 0.6% month-on-month against +0.1% consensus, the largest decline since May 2025, with the control group at -0.4% against +0.3% expected; the University of Michigan preliminary August sentiment index printed 51.0 against 55.2 prior and a 54.5-54.6 consensus. Company-level pressure was concentrated rather than broad: Broadcom fell about 6%, Applied Materials fell more than 5% despite guiding revenue above estimates, and Nvidia was effectively unchanged at 225.16.

Cross-asset, with one genuinely new element this hour. WTI settled at $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent at $88.52 (+1.67%), capping weekly gains of 5.4% and 6.0% respectively and year-on-year rises of roughly 33-34%, on the U.S. threat of an indefinite blockade and an IEA warning of the widest supply deficit in five years. The new datapoint is that a drone attack forced Russia's Sheskharis terminal at Novorossiysk to suspend crude exports, opening a second, Ukraine-Russia supply channel alongside Hormuz - two independent disruptions now bear on the same barrel. Analysts quoted in the reporting framed it plainly: a day of reckoning may come if Hormuz traffic, roughly 20% of global oil supply, stays constrained. On rates, the 10-year closed near 4.67% and the 2-year near 4.167% on Friday, against Federal Reserve H.15 constant maturities dated 13 August of 4.15% at 2 years, 4.63% at 10 years and 5.21% at 30 years - the H.15 values simply lag by a business day. The more telling datapoint remains that a 30-year auction cleared at 5.216%, the highest in 25 years, pointing to real long-end pressure alongside an otherwise calm equity tape.

Geopolitics remains the one live channel during the halt, and it hardened rather than eased into the weekend. The Strait of Hormuz is in roughly its 168th day of effective closure under a U.S. naval blockade, with transit counts near three-month lows against about 130 pre-conflict daily crossings. Negotiations are deadlocked: Iran's position is that while the blockade continues the conditions for reopening do not exist, and reporting describes no breakthrough on reviving the June interim deal. On the U.S. side, Defence Secretary Hegseth has vowed an indefinite blockade and Treasury Secretary Bessent said the administration will apply measures 'like have never been seen in the history of economic isolation of a country', describing a one-two punch of unprecedented sanctions plus continued port closure - and, importantly for timing, placing the announcement next week rather than this weekend.

Interpretation: the signals genuinely conflict, which is why this is scored as elevated Stress with low Tail rather than as either calm or dangerous. Equity volatility pricing near 14 with a tight day range, index levels close to records, a mid-range orderly Friday close, a small-cap record and a third straight weekly gain argue against imminent pathological structure. A closed chokepoint on day 168, two separate oil-supply disruptions, a 5-6% weekly crude rally, a sharp consumer-demand and sentiment miss, a 25-year-high long-bond auction yield and a confirmed unprecedented sanctions package argue that the environment is difficult and gap-prone. Per the contract, conflicting signals raise Stress rather than Tail, and Stress must not decay to a trivial floor merely because the venue is shut while the catalyst set is unresolved - hence 45% here. Tail remains low at 9% because not one of the required Tail conditions - observed persistent directional efficiency, shallow or failed pullbacks, repeated extension, NQ pinned near extremes - can be evidenced while no price is printing, and none was present at the last observable close.
lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 9-11% through the Asian and European sessions of Friday 14 August and easing to 7-9% across the U.S. cash session: the softer Retail Sales and University of Michigan prints and the Broadcom/Applied Materials drag produced two-way volatility and rotation into small caps, not directional efficiency. Stress described a clear event arc - roughly 23-29% in the quiet pre-dawn hours, building to 40-44% through the U.S. cash session as the data and semiconductor news landed, then 34% after the 21:00 UTC weekly close and collapsing to 12% in the two post-close halt runs, before being corrected back to 45-46% from 00:00 UTC onward. That correction is the reading carried forward here: the venue shut, but the Hormuz closure, the oil rally and the pending sanctions package did not resolve, so the backdrop never justified a trivial weekend floor. Confidence trended down through Friday from the high 40s to the low 30s as supplementary data coverage degraded, recovered to the 50s once primary-source reads succeeded from 13:00 UTC, and stood at 56% for the most recent completed hour. The 20:00 UTC slot has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable. Every past hour is reproduced exactly as it was published and is not restated with later information.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it ends at 01:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, still roughly 21 hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is therefore projected flat at 9% for the first eighteen slots, ticking to 10% from 20:00 UTC on 15 August as the reopen edges into view; this reflects accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays in the low band so the action is EA_ON green throughout. Stress is projected to ease from 45% to about 41% through the thin Saturday Asian and European hours, when Gulf-related headline flow is historically lightest, then firm back to 45-46% into the late slots as unresolved weekend headlines converge on the Sunday gap; it stays inside the elevated band all horizon because the Hormuz closure, the twin oil-supply disruptions, the consumer-demand miss and the confirmed Iran package are unresolved rather than because any event is scheduled. Confidence decays from 58% to 44% as Friday's verified evidence ages with nothing observable to replace it. The named danger window is the Sunday reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery, which sits just beyond this horizon; the first scheduled macro checkpoint is the Empire State survey on 17 August at 12:30 UTC and the only high-impact event in the seven-day window is FOMC Minutes on 19 August at 18:00 UTC, with the Jackson Hole symposium falling on 27-29 August, outside it.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour sits deep inside the CME weekend halt. The last quote was Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and nothing prints again until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, so directional efficiency, pullback depth and proximity to extremes are all unobservable. Tail 9% reflects that absence of a price path plus an orderly mid-range Friday close at 30,046.14 with VIX at 14.25; Stress 45% carries the day-168 Hormuz closure, a 5.4%/6.0% weekly WTI/Brent rally and the Iran economic-isolation package flagged for next week.

Still the CME halt, with Gulf headline flow the only live channel. Nothing on the U.S. calendar and no venue quoting, so Tail holds at 9% and the action stays EA_ON green. Stress unchanged at 45%: the Novorossiysk export suspension after a drone strike adds a second, Russia-side supply disruption on top of the Hormuz blockade, so the energy channel is not quieting.

Early Saturday, historically the thinnest window for Gulf and Washington headline flow. Tail 9%. Stress eases a point to 44% as the probability of a fresh market-moving statement inside this specific hour falls, not because any driver has resolved - the blockade, the oil rally and the pending sanctions package all remain open.

Weekend quiet continues with no price discovery anywhere. Tail 9%, EA_ON green. Stress 44%, still well inside the elevated band: Friday's 0.6% retail-sales drop and the 51.0 University of Michigan sentiment print are unresolved demand-side signals that the next cash session will have to re-price.

Saturday morning in Europe, with the U.S. calendar empty until Monday's Empire State survey. Tail 9%. Stress 43% - the slow drift lower prices the passage of an uneventful weekend hour, while the floor stays high because a 30-year auction cleared at 5.216%, the highest in 25 years, and the long end remains the one genuinely stressed market.

Mid-Saturday, roughly 16 hours before the CME reopen. Tail 9% with no observable structure to score; the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than any observed extension. Stress 43%, easing gently through the quiet stretch before firming again into the late slots as unresolved weekend headlines converge on the Sunday gap.
